examples.title: Remove a key and repair the root link
examples.explanationHtml: The root has two children. Its key becomes 9, then the old node containing 9 is unlinked and freed.

examples.title: Delete a one-child root
examples.explanationHtml: The root link receives the saved child pointer. Node 3 stays alive after node 8 is freed.

examples.title: Drain a tree through its minimum
examples.explanationHtml: Every minimum lacks a left child, so each removal uses the zero-child or one-child case. The final root is NULL.

practice.title: Delete a missing key
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12), n insertion keys (-99..99), then an int deletion key. Print Count and keys:, removed=0 or 1, then inorder: with remaining keys.
hints: An unsuccessful recursive search returns the original subtree.

practice.title: Repeated deletion requests
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12), insertion keys (-99..99), m (0..12), then m int deletion keys. Print Count and keys:, size=S after each request, then inorder: and the remaining keys.
hints: Keep assigning the returned root even when it becomes NULL.

practice.title: Trim keys outside an interval
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12), insertion keys (-99..99), and int low/high with low at most high. Print Count and keys: then inorder: containing only keys in the inclusive interval.
hints: Trim both children before removing an out-of-range root.

practice.title: Delete every leaf from the original shape
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12) and insertion keys (-99..99). Print Count and keys: then inorder: after deleting only nodes that were leaves before pruning began.
hints: Test leaf status before recursive calls change the children.

quiz.prompt: Which replacement removes a leaf node?
quiz.explanation: A leaf owns no child subtree, so its parent link becomes NULL.

quiz.prompt: What must be saved before freeing a one-child node?
options: The address of a freed member
quiz.explanation: Dereferencing the old node after free is invalid.

quiz.prompt: Which node supplies the common two-child replacement key?
quiz.explanation: The right minimum lies above every left key and at or below all remaining right keys.

quiz.prompt: Why can the successor node be removed using at most one child?
options: It must be the right-subtree root
quiz.explanation: A smaller left descendant would contradict its minimum status.

quiz.prompt: What happens when erase returns NULL after deleting the last root?
options: Assign NULL to the caller root
quiz.explanation: The caller must discard its pointer to the released node.

quiz.prompt: If a deletion key is absent, how should the BST change?
quiz.explanation: Reaching a NULL link ends the unsuccessful request.

quiz.prompt: After copying a successor key, how many physical nodes should a successful deletion free?
quiz.explanation: The target record stays; only the old successor record is released.

quiz.prompt: After promoting the only child and freeing the old root, which live key remains?
quiz.explanation: The child pointer is saved before free; the stack-allocated child remains alive.

quiz.prompt: Copying key 9 and then deleting its old record changes this key count by how much?
quiz.explanation: Copying changes a key value but only the physical deletion decreases the count, from seven to six.

quiz.prompt: Deleting the final leaf sets root to NULL. What emptiness value is printed?
quiz.explanation: The pointer is explicitly reset after releasing its allocation.

quiz.prompt: Why is setting a local pointer to NULL after free insufficient to repair the caller?
options: The caller has a separate pointer value
C passes all pointer variables by reference
quiz.explanation: Return the new subtree root or modify the actual owner link.

examQuestions.question: Insert 8,3,12,10,14,9,11, then delete 8 by successor replacement. Draw the changed links and identify the freed record.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The successor is 9, found through 12.left=10 and 10.left=9. Copy 9 into the original root record. Set 10.left to NULL and free the old 9 record. The root now stores 9; its left child remains 3 and its right subtree remains rooted at 12. Inorder becomes 3,9,10,11,12,14.

examQuestions.question: Write the at-most-one-child branch of erase and explain why its operation order matters.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Node *child = root->left != NULL ? root->left : root->right;
free(root);
return child;

Read the child while root is alive. The caller assigns the returned pointer into its owner link. Calling destroy(root) instead would wrongly release the surviving subtree; reading root members after free would use an ended lifetime.

examQuestions.question: Prove that the right-subtree minimum is a valid two-child deletion replacement.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Every left-subtree key is smaller than the old root, which is smaller than the successor. Every remaining right-subtree key is larger than that unique successor. Copying the successor therefore keeps both bounds after its original record is removed. The successor has no left child, so removing it requires at most one-child promotion.

examQuestions.question: State the time, auxiliary space and allocation effect of recursive BST deletion.
examQuestions.answerHtml: It follows one search path and possibly a successor path within that subtree: O(h+1) time and O(h+1) call space. No new records are allocated. A successful request frees one record; an absent-key request frees none. Worst-case height can be linear in n.

summary.en: Delete a BST key while preserving ordering, repairing links and freeing the removed node.
summary.bn: বিএসটির কী মুছে লিংক ঠিক করো, সার্চের নিয়ম রাখো আর বাদ যাওয়া নোডের মেমরি ছেড়ে দাও।
